ns2:section.sectionText: This course introduces the basic principles of quantum mechanics and its applications in modern electronics and quantum information science. The course covers three main topics: (i) the mathematical formalism of quantum mechanics and solutions to Schrödinger’s equation, (ii) semi-classical theory of light-matter interaction and quantum control, and (iii) qubits and principles of quantum information processing. Sub-topics studied in detail include finite versus infinite-dimensional quantum systems, bra/ket notation, quantum harmonic oscillator, crystalline structures and semi-conductors, atomic absorption and emission, Rabi oscillations, atomic qubits and the Bloch sphere, quantum entanglement, quantum gates and algorithms, quantum teleportation, and quantum key distribution. A primary goal of this course is to prepare the student for higher-level courses in quantum information science. Prerequisites: PHYS 214, ECE 329
